questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). Triangle ABC is to be constructed with AB = 80 mm, angle CAB = 60 degrees and angle ABC = 45 degrees, using compasses (no protractor).
(a) Name three drawing instruments needed for this construction. [3 marks]
(b) State, in order, the steps for constructing the 60 degree angle at A. [4 marks]
(c) State, in order, the steps for constructing the 45 degree angle at B. [4 marks]
(d) State the size of angle ACB and the expected lengths of AC and BC, each to the nearest millimetre. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Any three of: compasses, ruler/scale rule, sharp pencil, tee-square, drawing board (1 mark each)
4 marks: 60 degrees: draw AB 80 mm; arc from A cutting AB; same radius arc from that point cutting the first arc; join A through the intersection
4 marks: 45 degrees: construct a 90 degree angle (perpendicular) at B with arcs; bisect the right angle with equal arcs; join B through the bisector point
2 marks: Angle ACB = 75 degrees
1 mark: AC = 59 mm (58.6 mm; allow 58-60)
1 mark: BC = 72 mm (71.7 mm; allow 71-73)
questions.explanation: Instruments: compasses, ruler and pencil. For 60 degrees, draw an arc from A cutting AB at D; with the same radius and centre D, cut the arc at E; AE makes 60 degrees with AB. For 45 degrees, construct a perpendicular at B and bisect the 90 degree angle. The arms meet at C. Angle C = 180 - 60 - 45 = 75 degrees. By the sine rule, AC = 80 x sin 45 / sin 75 = 58.6 mm and BC = 80 x sin 60 / sin 75 = 71.7 mm.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). Triangle PQR has PQ = 70 mm, QR = 60 mm and PR = 50 mm. A circle is to be drawn passing through P, Q and R.
(a) State, in order, the steps for constructing triangle PQR from its three sides. [4 marks]
(b) What name is given to a circle that passes through all three corners of a triangle? [2 marks]
(c) State how the centre of this circle is located. [4 marks]
(d) State the expected radius of the circle to the nearest millimetre. [3 marks]
(e) Name the instrument used to draw the circle. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Draw PQ = 70 mm
1 mark: With centre P and radius 50 mm draw an arc
1 mark: With centre Q and radius 60 mm draw an arc cutting the first arc at R
1 mark: Join PR and QR
2 marks: Circumscribed circle (circumcircle)
2 marks: Construct the perpendicular bisectors of any two sides
2 marks: The point where they meet is the centre (circumcentre)
3 marks: Radius = 36 mm (35.7 mm; allow 35-37)
2 marks: Compasses
questions.explanation: Draw PQ, swing arcs of 50 mm from P and 60 mm from Q to meet at R. The circle through all three corners is the circumscribed circle; its centre is where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet. Using radius = (product of sides) / (4 x area): area = 1469.7 mm2, so R = 70 x 60 x 50 / 5878.8 = 35.7 mm. The circle is drawn with compasses.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A regular hexagon is to be constructed inside a circle of radius 40 mm, with its corners on the circle.
(a) State, in order, the steps for constructing the hexagon. [5 marks]
(b) Explain why this method gives six equal sides. [2 marks]
(c) State the length of each side of the hexagon. [2 marks]
(d) State the expected distance across the flats to the nearest millimetre. [3 marks]
(e) State the size of each interior angle of the hexagon. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Draw a circle of radius 40 mm
2 marks: Keep the compasses at 40 mm and step off from any point round the circumference
1 mark: Six equally spaced points are obtained
1 mark: Join the points with straight lines
2 marks: The side of a regular hexagon equals the radius of its circumscribing circle (six equilateral triangles)
2 marks: Side = 40 mm
3 marks: Across flats = 69 mm (40 x square root of 3 = 69.3 mm; allow 68-70)
3 marks: Each interior angle = 120 degrees
questions.explanation: Draw the circle, keep the compasses at the radius and step round the circumference to get six points, then join them. The hexagon is made of six equilateral triangles, so each side equals the radius, 40 mm. Across the flats = 40 x 1.732 = 69.3 mm. Interior angle = (6 - 2) x 180 / 6 = 120 degrees.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A regular pentagon ABCDE of side 45 mm is to be constructed.
(a) Calculate the size of each interior angle of a regular pentagon, showing your working. [3 marks]
(b) State, in order, the steps for constructing the pentagon using a protractor to set out the angles. [6 marks]
(c) Name two instruments, apart from the protractor, used in the construction. [2 marks]
(d) State the expected length of the diagonal AC to the nearest millimetre. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Sum of interior angles = (5 - 2) x 180 = 540 degrees
1 mark: Each angle = 540 / 5 = 108 degrees
1 mark: Draw AB = 45 mm
2 marks: At A and at B set out angles of 108 degrees and mark AE = 45 mm and BC = 45 mm
2 marks: From C and E draw arcs of radius 45 mm to meet at D
1 mark: Join CD and DE to complete the pentagon
2 marks: Any two of: ruler, compasses, pencil, set square (1 mark each)
4 marks: AC = 73 mm (45 x 1.618 = 72.8 mm; allow 72-74)
questions.explanation: Interior angle = (5 - 2) x 180 / 5 = 108 degrees. Draw AB, set off 108 degrees at A and B, mark 45 mm along each arm to get E and C, then arcs of 45 mm from C and E meet at D. The diagonal of a regular pentagon is the side x 1.618 (the golden ratio), so AC = 72.8 mm.

questions.stem:

(a) State, in order, the steps for constructing the 90 degree angle at Y using compasses. [4 marks]
(b) Calculate the length of XZ. [3 marks]

1 mark: Extend XY beyond Y (or use Y as centre) and draw an arc cutting the line on both sides of Y
1 mark: From the two cut points draw equal arcs (radius larger than before) to intersect
1 mark: Join Y to the intersection to get the perpendicular
1 mark: Mark YZ = 60 mm along the perpendicular
1 mark: XZ squared = 80 squared + 60 squared = 10000
2 marks: XZ = 100 mm
2 marks: Inscribed circle (incircle)
2 marks: Centre is where the bisectors of the angles meet

questions.explanation: Construct the perpendicular at Y with equal arcs and mark YZ = 60 mm. By Pythagoras, XZ = square root of (6400 + 3600) = 100 mm. The inscribed circle's centre (incentre) is where the angle bisectors meet. r = area / semi-perimeter = 2400 / 120 = 20 mm.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A circle of radius 35 mm has centre O. Point P lies outside the circle such that OP = 80 mm. Two tangents are to be drawn from P to the circle.
(a) Define a tangent to a circle. [2 marks]
(b) State, in order, the steps for constructing the two tangents from P. [6 marks]
(c) State the angle between a tangent and the radius at the point of contact. [2 marks]
(d) Calculate the length of one tangent from P to its point of contact, to the nearest millimetre. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A straight line that touches a circle at only one point
2 marks: Join OP and bisect it to find its midpoint M
2 marks: With centre M and radius MO draw a circle/arc cutting the given circle at T1 and T2
2 marks: Join PT1 and PT2; these are the tangents
2 marks: 90 degrees
2 marks: PT squared = OP squared - OT squared = 6400 - 1225 = 5175
3 marks: PT = 72 mm (71.9 mm; allow 71-73)
questions.explanation: Bisect OP at M and draw a circle on OP as diameter; it cuts the given circle at T1 and T2. The angle in a semicircle is 90 degrees, so OT is perpendicular to PT, making PT a tangent. By Pythagoras, PT = square root of (80 squared - 35 squared) = square root of 5175 = 71.9 mm.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A line AB, 110 mm long, is to be divided into seven equal parts by a geometrical method (not by measuring).
(a) State, in order, the steps for dividing AB into seven equal parts. [6 marks]
(b) Name two instruments used to draw the parallel lines. [2 marks]
(c) State the length of one part to one decimal place. [3 marks]
(d) State the geometrical principle on which the method is based. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Draw AB = 110 mm
1 mark: Draw a line AC from A at a convenient acute angle
2 marks: Step off seven equal lengths along AC with compasses or dividers
1 mark: Join the seventh point to B
1 mark: Draw lines through the other points parallel to this line to cut AB
2 marks: Set squares and tee-square (or two set squares) (1 mark each)
3 marks: 110 / 7 = 15.7 mm
4 marks: Parallel lines divide two transversals in the same ratio (similar triangles / proportional division)
questions.explanation: Draw AC at an acute angle from A, step off seven equal units, join the last point to B and slide a set square along a straight edge to draw parallels through the other points. Each part is 110 / 7 = 15.7 mm. This works because parallel lines cut the two lines in the same ratio.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A regular octagon is to be constructed inside a square ABCD of side 60 mm by drawing arcs from each corner with a radius equal to half the diagonal.
(a) State, in order, the steps for this construction. [5 marks]
(b) Calculate half the diagonal of the square, to one decimal place. [3 marks]
(c) Calculate the length of one side of the octagon, to one decimal place. [4 marks]
(d) State the size of each interior angle of a regular octagon. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Construct the square ABCD of side 60 mm
1 mark: Draw the two diagonals to find the centre O
2 marks: With each corner as centre and radius equal to half the diagonal (AO), draw arcs cutting the two adjacent sides
1 mark: Join the eight points on the sides to form the octagon
1 mark: Diagonal = 60 x square root of 2 = 84.9 mm
2 marks: Half diagonal = 42.4 mm
2 marks: Each arc cuts a side 60 - 42.4 = 17.6 mm from the far corner
2 marks: Octagon side = 60 - 2 x 17.6 = 24.9 mm
3 marks: Each interior angle = 135 degrees
questions.explanation: Draw the square and its diagonals. From each corner swing an arc of radius AO = 42.4 mm to cut the adjacent sides, then join the eight points. Each cut leaves 17.6 mm at the end of a side, so the octagon side is 60 - 35.1 = 24.9 mm (equal to 60 x (square root of 2 - 1)). Interior angle = (8 - 2) x 180 / 8 = 135 degrees.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Kemi has typed a short notice in Microsoft Word with the heading CLEAN ENVIRONMENT CLUB followed by one paragraph.
(a) List, in order, the steps or commands to make the heading bold, centred and font size 16. [6 marks]
(b) State the commands to change the paragraph to Times New Roman, size 12, and justify it. [4 marks]
(c) State the keyboard shortcut used to underline selected text. [2 marks]
(d) List the steps to save the document with the name CLUB. [4 marks]
(e) Name the menu or tab and command used to print the document. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Select (highlight) the heading
1 mark: Click Bold on the Home tab or press Ctrl + B
1 mark: Click Center or press Ctrl + E
2 marks: Choose 16 from the Font Size box
2 marks: Select the paragraph and choose Times New Roman and size 12 from the font boxes
2 marks: Click Justify or press Ctrl + J
2 marks: Ctrl + U
1 mark: Click File (or press Ctrl + S / F12)
1 mark: Choose Save As
1 mark: Type CLUB in the File name box
1 mark: Click Save
2 marks: File tab (or Ctrl + P)
2 marks: Print command, then click Print
questions.explanation: Select the heading, press Ctrl + B, Ctrl + E and pick 16 in the Font Size box. Select the paragraph, choose Times New Roman, 12, then Justify (Ctrl + J). Ctrl + U underlines. File > Save As, type CLUB, click Save. File > Print (Ctrl + P), then click Print.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). A class result is entered in Microsoft Excel. Row 1 holds the headings NAME, MATHS, ENGLISH, BST in columns A to D. Rows 2 to 6 hold:
Adaeze 72, 65, 80
Bello 58, 70, 64
Chidi 85, 78, 90
Damilola 49, 55, 61
Efe 66, 81, 73
(a) Write the formula in cell E2 to find Adaeze's total using a function. [3 marks]
(b) State how the formula can be copied to E3:E6 without retyping. [2 marks]
(c) State the totals that will appear in E2 to E6. [5 marks]
(d) Write the formula in cell F2 to find Adaeze's average. [3 marks]
(e) State Chidi's average correct to 2 decimal places. [3 marks]
(f) Write the formula that finds the highest total in E2:E6 and state its result. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: =SUM(B2:D2)
2 marks: Drag the fill handle of E2 down to E6 (or copy and paste)
5 marks: 217, 192, 253, 165, 220 (1 mark each)
3 marks: =AVERAGE(B2:D2) (accept =E2/3)
3 marks: 84.33
2 marks: =MAX(E2:E6)
2 marks: 253
questions.explanation: E2: =SUM(B2:D2), then drag the fill handle down. Totals: Adaeze 217, Bello 192, Chidi 253, Damilola 165, Efe 220. F2: =AVERAGE(B2:D2). Chidi: 253 / 3 = 84.33. =MAX(E2:E6) returns 253.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Mrs Bassey's weekly sales are in Excel. Columns A, B and C hold ITEM, QUANTITY and UNIT PRICE (N); rows 2 to 6 hold: Sugar 12, 1500; Milk 24, 850; Bread 15, 1200; Soap 30, 450; Detergent 10, 2300.
(a) Write the formula in D2 to find the amount for Sugar. [2 marks]
(b) State the amounts that will appear in D2 to D6. [5 marks]
(c) Write the formula in D7 for the total amount and state its result. [4 marks]
(d) She gives a 5% discount on the total. Write a formula for the discount in D8 and state its value. [3 marks]
(e) List the steps to create a column chart of ITEM against AMOUNT titled WEEKLY SALES. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: =B2*C2
5 marks: 18000, 20400, 18000, 13500, 23000 (1 mark each)
2 marks: =SUM(D2:D6)
2 marks: 92900
2 marks: =D7*5% (or =D7*0.05)
1 mark: 4645
2 marks: Select A1:A6, then hold Ctrl and select D1:D6
2 marks: Insert tab > Column (chart) and choose a column chart
2 marks: Click the chart title and type WEEKLY SALES
questions.explanation: D2: =B2*C2 copied down gives 18000, 20400, 18000, 13500 and 23000. D7: =SUM(D2:D6) = 92900. Discount: =D7*0.05 = 4645. To chart, select the ITEM and AMOUNT columns (Ctrl for the second range), Insert > Column chart, then edit the title to WEEKLY SALES.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Tobi wants to draw a simple house in Microsoft Paint.
(a) Name the tool or shape used to draw the walls and the roof. [4 marks]
(b) Name the tool used to colour the walls yellow, and state how a colour is chosen. [4 marks]
(c) Name the tool used to type the words MY HOME below the house. [3 marks]
(d) Name the tool used to rub out a wrong line. [2 marks]
(e) Name the tool used to pick a colour already on the drawing. [3 marks]
(f) List the steps to save the picture as HOUSE. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Rectangle shape for the walls
2 marks: Triangle shape (or line tool) for the roof
2 marks: Fill with colour (paint bucket) tool
2 marks: Click the colour (yellow) on the colour palette before filling
3 marks: Text tool (A)
2 marks: Eraser
3 marks: Colour picker
1 mark: Click File
1 mark: Choose Save As
1 mark: Type HOUSE as the file name
1 mark: Click Save
questions.explanation: Walls: Rectangle shape; roof: Triangle shape or Line tool. Choose yellow on the palette and click inside the walls with Fill with colour. Text tool (A) for MY HOME, Eraser to remove errors, Colour picker to reuse a colour. Save with File > Save As, type HOUSE, click Save.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Ada is designing an invitation card for her school's inter-house sports in CorelDRAW.
(a) Name the tool used to draw the rectangular border, and state how its exact size (15 cm by 10 cm) can be set. [4 marks]
(b) Name the tool used to type the heading INTER-HOUSE SPORTS. [3 marks]
(c) State how to fill a drawn shape with colour. [3 marks]
(d) Name the tool used to draw a round ball shape. [3 marks]
(e) Name the tool used to select and move objects. [3 marks]
(f) State two other examples of graphic packages. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Rectangle tool
2 marks: Type width 15 cm and height 10 cm in the property bar
3 marks: Text tool
3 marks: Select the shape and click a colour on the colour palette (or use the Fill tool)
3 marks: Ellipse tool (hold Ctrl for a perfect circle)
3 marks: Pick tool (selection arrow)
4 marks: Any two of: Paint, Adobe Photoshop, GIMP, Instant Artist, Adobe Illustrator (2 marks each)
questions.explanation: The Rectangle tool draws the border; the property bar sets its exact width and height. The Text tool types the heading. Select a shape and click a palette colour to fill it. The Ellipse tool (with Ctrl) draws a circle, and the Pick tool selects and moves objects. Other graphic packages include Paint, Photoshop and GIMP.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Musa wants to type a Monday timetable in Microsoft Word as a table with the columns PERIOD, TIME and SUBJECT, a heading row and four periods.
(a) How many columns and rows will the table need? [2 marks]
(b) List the steps to insert the table. [5 marks]
(c) State the key used to move from one cell to the next. [2 marks]
(d) List the steps to make the first row bold and shade it light grey. [5 marks]
(e) State the keyboard shortcuts for: (i) saving the document; (ii) undoing a mistake; (iii) copying selected text. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: 3 columns and 5 rows
1 mark: Place the cursor where the table is wanted
2 marks: Click the Insert tab, then Table
2 marks: Choose 3 columns and 5 rows (or Insert Table and type the numbers) and click OK
2 marks: Tab key
1 mark: Select the first row
2 marks: Press Ctrl + B (or click Bold)
2 marks: Use Shading (Table Design tab) and choose light grey
2 marks: Ctrl + S
2 marks: Ctrl + Z
2 marks: Ctrl + C
questions.explanation: One heading row plus four periods needs 5 rows and 3 columns. Insert > Table, choose 3 x 5. Tab moves between cells. Select row 1, Ctrl + B, then Table Design > Shading > light grey. Shortcuts: Ctrl + S save, Ctrl + Z undo, Ctrl + C copy.
